method: Pre-war trend per country and flow, used to build a counterfactual baseline for 2022-2026. Data: UN Comtrade public preview (HS TOTAL, annual, 2012-2021; 2002-2013 for the back-test), each economy's own report; missing years from the partner's report (Russia's or Ukraine's), scaled by the country's median own/partner ratio over overlapping years (generic CIF/FOB ratios 0.847/1.320/0.810/1.388 as in trade_full.json when fewer than 3 overlaps). USD converted to EUR with ECB annual averages. Real terms: imports from Russia deflated with a fixed-weight index from the 2019-2021 fuel mix (energy2.json fuel_mix_2019_2021; import-weighted average mix for other countries; pipeline-gas index for Europe/CIS/China, LNG index elsewhere); other flows with the non-fuel goods index. 2019-2021 index values are energy2.json central; 2012-2018 are back-cast by chaining onto the 2019-2021 mean with Brent (crude), ULSD NY Harbor (products), IMF EU gas price (pipeline gas), Japan LNG, Newcastle coal (all in EUR) and, for non-fuel goods, the geometric mean of the euro-area import price index for industrial products excluding energy and the US non-fuel import price index in EUR. Deflator sensitivity: refit with (A) Eurostat EA import price indices for every component and (B) US non-fuel import prices in EUR; the larger shift is added to the band. Fit: OLS of log real value on year. Window choice, per series: if 2012-2013 sit significantly off the post-2016 line (dummy |coef|>0.20 log, |t|>2) the 2016-2021 post-Crimea regime is used ('break_2014'); else if 2014-2015 lie >0.10 log and >2 residual SD below the line through the other years they are left out ('shock_2014_15'); else all of 2012-2021. One gross outlier (>0.40 log and >3 SD) may be dropped. 2020 (COVID) is kept. g band = central +/- sqrt((t95,df x SE)^2 + deflator shift^2) (roughly a 90% interval for the slope), widened where needed to include the central slopes of the other two windows (window uncertainty); it is not an interval for year-to-year noise. For importers whose customs omit Russian pipeline gas (DEU, AUT, POL, NLD, FRA, HUN, CHE, FIN, BEL, TUR) the import trend is a weighted mix of the non-gas customs trend (TOTAL minus HS 2711) and Gazprom's Europe+Turkey delivery volume trend 2012-2021, weighted by the 2019-2021 gas share in energy2.json. Multiplier(Y) = counterfactual real value in year Y relative to the 2019-2021 real average (anchored at 2020): exp(g0 + sum_{y=2022..Y} g0 x 0.5^((y-2021)/H)), where g0 is the log trend growth capped to [ln 0.9, ln 1.1]; 2021 carries the full in-sample trend. Applies to real values (pre-war prices); multiply the 2019-2021 real baseline by it, then by the year's price index for a nominal counterfactual.

damping.justification: Back-test on the same data one cycle earlier (2002-2007 trends, 291 country-flows above EUR 50m, anchored on 2005-2007, scored on 2008 and 2010-2013): median absolute log error 0.77 for the undamped trend, 0.41 for a flat baseline (no trend), 0.36 for an undamped trend capped at +/-10%, and 0.31-0.33 for half-lives of 2-5 years with a +/-10% cap (H=3: 0.318, median bias +0.05; H=2: 0.311; H=5: 0.328). The error surface is flat between H=2 and H=5, so H=3 is the middle of the near-optimal range; a +/-10% cap was never worse than wider caps for H>=2. With H=3 the total trend effect is limited: a series growing >=10%/yr reaches at most x1.41 in 2026 (x0.68 for >=10%/yr decline). This matches the damped-trend forecasting literature (Gardner & McKenzie 1985; damping parameters of about 0.8 per year, i.e. half-lives of 3 years, are typical for annual macro series).
damping.use_for_unreliable: For series with reliable=false, the suggested central is 1.0 (flat 2019-2021 baseline) while the low/high multipliers show what the trend could imply; the multiplier fields themselves are computed from the fit for every series.
damping.forecast_error_note: The low/high band reflects only slope and deflator uncertainty. In the back-test the typical (median) error of the damped trend in an individual country-flow after 4-7 years was about 0.3 log (x/÷1.35), so individual counterfactual values are rough.
